title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Lanthanide complexes can construct C–N bonds from CO2 and 2-aminobenzonitriles or aziridines under milder conditions than many transition-metal systems because their metal–ligand interactions are weakly covalent, labile, and nondirectional, allowing substrates to approach from multiple directions.
explanation: Amidato Ln2 clusters (Eu, Yb) convert 2-aminobenzonitrile and CO2 to quinazolinediones at ambient pressure, and a related Eu cluster cycloadds aziridines. The proposed aziridine path begins with CO2 and aziridine coordination at Lewis-acidic europium to form the active complex.
scope: Amidato dinuclear Eu and Yb clusters for CO2 cycloaddition to 2-aminobenzonitriles or aziridines.
conditions: Eu2a: DBU, 100 °C, 0.1 MPa, 24 h, 91% yield; Eu2b: DBU, 50 °C, 0.1 MPa, 48 h, 90% yield.
caveats: The directional-approach argument is a general lanthanide bonding rationale illustrated by these clusters, not a quantified comparison across all transition-metal catalysts.
